title: [seam -> repo:objectui] the confirm card should send back the IDENTITY of the blueprint it rendered — the runtime's receiving side is already built and is the last gap in the consent gate (cloud#2006)
body:
Blocked-by: nothing — this is the missing half, not a dependency

Filed by the `repo:cloud` execution seat (objectstack#6026) from cloud#2006's first triage, 2026-09-16. Cross-board card because the fix is a UI-to-runtime contract and cannot be made inside the `apply_blueprint` handler; the cloud seat correctly did not force it into its own file surface.

## What is already done, on the runtime side

cloud#1954 (PR #2005) changed the consent gate's question from "does this turn look like an approval?" to "is this the blueprint the user confirmed?". Two of the three gaps closed. The receiving side for the identity exists and is tested — verified in a cloud checkout at ref `cb8ee7ff60c097cc21a584fe9caf8ef4391cc0e8` on 2026-09-16:

- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/tools/confirm-gate.ts:124` reads `confirmedBlueprintIdentity` off the execution context;
- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/tools/blueprint-tools.ts:295` documents that it comes off the persisted conversation;
- six cases in `__tests__/blueprint-tools.test.ts` drive it (lines 4370, 4463, 4534, 4566, 4681).

## The gap this card closes

When the route does not forward the user's text (`hasUserMessageText` is false — `confirm-gate.ts:28-31`), the gate can only fall back to `presentedInPriorTurn`. A conversation that once showed a proposal card can therefore apply a blueprint **the user never saw**.

The durable fix is not another heuristic on the runtime side: the confirm click has to arrive as an identifiable event. **The card already holds the blueprint when it renders it** — sending that identity back with the click is the whole change, and the runtime's receiver is waiting for it.

## Why it is not urgent

The production console uses the text-forwarding path; the blind route is a test-environment shape. cloud#1954 narrowed the exposure from "any later turn" to "only when the route genuinely forwarded no text". ⚠️ Not urgent is not the same as not real: the gate's guarantee is currently conditional on a routing detail rather than on the user's action.

## Suggested timing

After v1, together with objectui's confirm card work — the card renders the blueprint, so carrying its identity on the click is a small addition at that point and an awkward retrofit at any other.

## ⚠️ One thing to check before designing

`confirm-gate.ts:26` records that `hasUserMessageText` "AUTO-ACTIVATES once the service-ai to cloud migration wires the text in". If that migration lands first, the blind-route case may close on its own and this card becomes belt-and-braces rather than the fix. Worth confirming that migration's state before spending design effort here — and if it has landed, say so on cloud#2006 rather than closing this silently.

## Related

cloud#2006 (the cloud-side card, `pm:blocked` on this one) · cloud#1954 / PR #2005 (the runtime-side gate) · `ToolExecutionContext.confirmedBlueprintIdentity` (the receiver)
